text:
If you're heading out for the evening, don't put the umbrella away just yet. That special weather statement earlier tracks with what's still bubbling up out there, scattered showers and thunderstorms lingering into tonight, with some capable of dumping heavier rain fast, so isolated flash flooding isn't out of the question. Sun's already down as of a few minutes ago, and the muggy 84-degree, feels-like-90 air sticks around into the evening with lows only dropping to near 69. The Euro and ICON models are notably wetter than the American model tonight, and given the thunderstorm activity already around, I'd side with them, so keep the rain gear handy if you're out late.

Sunday flips the script. A cold front clears things out overnight, and behind it we're looking at sunshine, a high near 85, and humidity finally backing off. There's a small chance of lingering showers up along the Canadian border and northern high ground, but Burlington proper should be dry and comfortable. Good day building toward for any outdoor plans, and the lake turns clean and glassy behind the front too.

ALERTS: Special Weather Statement issued August 8 at 4:38PM EDT by NWS Burlington VT

  Tonight: Scattered showers and thunderstorms before 5am. Partly cloudy, with a low around 69. South wind 3 to 7 mph. Chance of precipitation is 40%. New rainfall amounts between a tenth and quarter of an inch possible.
  Sunday: Sunny, with a high near 85. West wind around 8 mph. New rainfall amounts less than a tenth of an inch possible.
  Sunday Night: Partly cloudy, with a low around 65. Southwest wind 2 to 7 mph.
AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-08-08T18:26:00+00:00):
  1. Intervals of showers and thunderstorms will continue this afternoon and evening. Warm and humid conditions will persist through much of the weekend.
  2. Chances for heavier showers and thunderstorms continue to look likely Monday into Tuesday as a shortwave pushes through the region.
  3. Unsettled weather continues Wednesday onward, and temperatures trend slightly below normal by the weekend.
AFD WHAT CHANGED: As of 223 PM EDT Saturday... Have increased chances for precipitation slightly on Sunday on northern and western slopes of the Adirondacks as well as northern Vermont along the international border due to cold pool/upslope type rain showers and thunderstorms. Have also incorporated patchy fog in valley locations to the forecast tonight and Sunday night.

  Sunday Night: Northwest winds 10 knots or less, becoming south. Mostly clear. Waves 1 foot or less.
  Monday: South winds 10 to 15 knots, increasing to 15 to 20 knots. Partly sunny. A chance of showers in the afternoon. Waves 1 to 2 feet.

  high None, low 69: Showers and thunderstorms early. Lows overnight in the upper 60s.
  high 86, low 64: Times of sun and clouds. Highs in the mid 80s and lows in the mid 60s.
WCAX METEOROLOGIST: BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Scattered showers and thunderstorms will continue today, but they will be more widely scattered compared to last night. Severe weather isn’t expected, but there could be locally an inch or more of rain in any thunderstorms with isolated flash flooding not out of the question. A cold front will come through tonight and into Sunday, leaving us with just the chance for a few showers or thunderstorms in the Northeast Kingdom on Sunday. The humidity will be kicked down a notch Sunday afternoon. High temperatures over the weekend will be in the 80s.
